about: The workforce of the server this repository is deployed to. Read by scripts/host/workforce.py (Deploy workflow: workforce-plan, workforce); the format is in scripts/host/README.md.

Sixteen teams, each for one kind of work and each with a workflow: software, short reels, product videos, brochures and catalogues, online stores, landing pages, Minecraft plugins, Bedrock add-ons, Minecraft server setups, custom Minecraft features, Pterodactyl installations, Discord bots, social media carousels, SEO articles, proposals, and work on Xiero Nexus AI itself. A team's description names its workflow.

Skills are in skills/ next to this file, a folder with a SKILL.md each: the way each kind of work is done here. The program puts them into the app and gives them to the agents and teams named below; an agent reads its own skills and its team's with every task. Edit a SKILL.md and run the workforce action with --update to change a skill; one that was changed on the Skills page is overwritten by that.

Three skills are the owner's own and are not in this repository: xiero-premium-web-studio, xiero-nexus-ai and xiero-minecraft-forge ("uploaded": true below). They are uploaded on the Skills page, or sealed for the node with the workforce action; the teams that name them get them when the app has them, and are made without them until then. A skill that a team or an agent was given by hand on its page is kept: this file adds skills and takes none away.

The agents write documents and files into a project's workspace. They do not compile, start a game, or touch a customer's server: the server has no sandbox runner. Every workflow therefore ends with a test list, a checklist or a review for a person, and says what was not run.

Everything here costs nothing. The providers Kilo Gateway, OVHcloud AI Endpoints, LLM7 and Pollinations take no key; the program adds them. The two Gemini models are the ones a key without billing can use: the voice, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, which answers slowly on that tier and is the second model of the two agents that write for readers.

What costs nothing is limited: Kilo Gateway to 200 requests an hour from one address by its documentation (when it was counted on this server, to about a hundred), OVHcloud to 2 requests a minute for each model, LLM7 to a daily allowance that a few tasks use up. From version 1.6 the app waits and asks again when a provider says "too many requests"; before that, such an answer ended the attempt.

Every agent has a quick first model with Kilo Gateway, and a second with another provider, most with OVHcloud, whose models are open ones that stay. No agent depends on LLM7: without a key its allowance for a day lasts a few tasks. Its free models (codestral-latest and gpt-oss:20b answered) are in the app to be picked by hand. Free pools change: a model that is gone answers with an error, the agent goes on with its second model, and --test says which one it was. When Kilo Gateway's allowance is used up, every agent works on its second model: that was seen on this server, and a project that takes a minute and a half took ten.
gpt-oss-120b of OVHcloud is no agent's model: it is the one to pick as the manager model of a project, which plans, sums up, and is every task's last resort. "tryRun" uses it that way.
What is sent to the free models of Kilo Gateway and LLM7 may be logged by the provider and used to improve its models: nothing personal or confidential.

The free image model (Stable Diffusion XL at OVHcloud) makes square pictures of 1024 by 1024 only, and takes between ten seconds and a minute and a half for one, so the reel shows them cropped to its vertical frame.

Two models that were tried and did not serve are switched off: one was rate-limited by its provider, the other took four minutes to answer. Qwen3.5-397B of OVHcloud is left out: it answered one word in seconds at times, and not within five minutes at another.
The app waits up to 300 seconds for an answer of a provider instead of 60: an agent's request is answered in one piece.
The try-run plans a small goal with the plugin team and gives each agent of that team one task: every agent of the file would be more requests than the free tiers allow in an hour.

With --only-usable the workforce action also switches off the models that cannot be used: those a provider without a key bills for, and those a provider refuses one word. The models named here are never switched off by it.

Kilo Gateway.notes: Free models, no key. Its documentation allows 200 requests an hour from one address, for all its models together; on this server it answered "sign up for free or come back later" after about a hundred. The agents then go on with their second models, slowly. A free account at kilo.ai gives a key. The free models change often, and those hosted by NVIDIA are busy at times. What is sent may be logged and used to improve models: nothing personal or confidential.

OVHcloud AI Endpoints.notes: Open models hosted in the EU, no key. 2 requests a minute for each model from one address.

LLM7.notes: Free models, no key, for picking by hand: 1 request a second, and an allowance for a day that a few tasks use up, so no agent depends on it. Its documentation gives a free token 100,000 tokens a day. Most of the models it lists need its paid plan. What is sent may be logged and used to improve models: nothing personal or confidential.

Pollinations.notes: The old open text API of Pollinations, no key: one chat model (GPT-OSS 20B), one request at a time from one address. Its newer API takes a key and is billed.

agents.name: Manager
instructions: Turns a goal into a delivery plan: scope, milestones, tasks with an owner and acceptance criteria, dependencies and risks. Tracks status and unblocks the team.
How you work:
- Start from the outcome the user wants. Say what is in scope and what is not.

- Break the work into tasks small enough for one specialist. Name the owner by role (Designer, Frontend, Backend, Tester, QA, Security Engineer, DevOps, Short Reels, Copywriter), what the task depends on, and an acceptance criterion that can be checked.
- List risks, assumptions and open questions. Give every open question a default decision, so that work can go on.
- Status reports: done, in progress, blocked, next steps, decisions needed. Short tables or lists, no filler.
- You do not do the specialists' work (no code, no design); you check their output against the criteria and say what is missing.

steps.title: Product brief
steps.objective: Write the product brief for the project goal: the problem and who has it, the target users, the goals and the non-goals, the smallest version worth shipping (what is in and what is out), the success metrics, and the main risks. Where the goal leaves a choice open, decide, and say why.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Problem, users, goals, non-goals, the scope of the first version, success metrics and risks; every open choice is decided.

steps.title: Delivery plan
steps.objective: Turn the brief into a delivery plan: the milestones; the tasks of each role (Designer, Backend, Frontend, Tester, Security Engineer, QA, DevOps) with what each depends on and its acceptance criteria; the technical stack (what the goal names, otherwise a common and simple one, with the reason); the risks and what to do about each; the open questions, each with a default decision.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Tasks with an owner, an order and acceptance criteria; a named stack; risks; no open question without a default.

steps.objective: Design what the user sees: the main user flows step by step; each screen (layout, components, and the states empty, loading, error and success); the design tokens (colours, type scale, spacing, radius, shadows) with exact values; how it behaves on small and large screens; the accessibility requirements. Write it so that the Frontend can build it without guessing.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Flows, every screen with its states, tokens with exact values, responsive behaviour and accessibility requirements.

steps.title: API and data design
steps.objective: Design the server side: the data model (entities, fields, relations, indexes); the API (for each endpoint: method, path, request, response, errors, and who may call it); the rules of authentication and authorization; the validation rules.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A data model and a complete list of endpoints with request, response, errors and access rule for each.

steps.title: Backend implementation
steps.objective: Implement the server side as the API and data design says, in the stack of the delivery plan: write complete, working files into the project workspace (code, configuration, migrations, tests). Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Every endpoint of the design is implemented with validation and access checks; there are tests for the main paths; no placeholders.

steps.title: Frontend implementation
steps.objective: Implement the user interface as the design says, against the API of the API and data design, in the stack of the delivery plan: write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Every screen of the design is built with its loading, empty and error states and calls the API as designed; no placeholders.

steps.title: Test plan and automated tests
steps.objective: Write the test plan: cases with steps and expected results for the main flows, the boundaries and the failure cases. Add automated tests to the workspace for what the Backend and the Frontend built. Run them when you can run commands; otherwise say that they were not run. The deliverable is the test plan, with the list of test files and the result of the run.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A test plan that covers the main flows and failure cases, automated tests in the workspace, and a clear statement of whether they were run.

steps.title: Security review
steps.objective: Review the design and the files in the workspace for security: authentication and sessions, access control on every route and object, input handling and injection, XSS, CSRF and SSRF, secrets, dependencies, sensitive data in logs and errors. List the findings by severity, each with where it is, the risk, and the concrete fix. Say what you could not review.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings ranked by severity with location, risk and fix; a statement of what was and was not reviewed.

steps.title: QA review
steps.objective: Check the result against the product brief and the acceptance criteria of each step: read the files in the workspace, compare the frontend with the API and with the design, and list the defects by severity with where each is and how to fix it. End with a verdict: ready, ready with conditions, or not ready.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Defects by severity with location and fix, and a verdict with the conditions for passing.

steps.title: Release plan
steps.objective: Write how this is built, configured, deployed and rolled back: the environment variables, the build and start commands, a Dockerfile or a deployment script as files in the workspace where that fits, health checks, backups, monitoring, and a release checklist that takes in the open findings of the security review and the QA review.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Build, configuration, deployment and rollback steps that can be followed, and a release checklist that names the open findings.

steps.title: Plan, format and art direction
steps.objective: Plan the printed piece for the project goal. Give: (1) its job: what the reader should do after reading; (2) the format, with the reason: page size in millimetres, number of pages or panels, where it will be read; (3) the page plan: for each page or panel, what goes on it, in order; (4) the content inventory: every product or service named in the goal with the facts given for it, and a list of what is missing as TODO(client); (5) the direction in one sentence and what it rules out; (6) the tokens: colours with hex values and a job each, one accent; type sizes in points for headings, body, captions and prices; the grid (columns, gutters, margins in millimetres); (7) the three pictures needed (cover, product, detail or in use): what each shows, and one style line that all three share.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A job, a format in millimetres, a plan for every page or panel, an inventory with TODO(client) for every gap, a direction, tokens with exact values, and three pictures with one shared style line. Nothing invented.

steps.title: Copy
steps.objective: Write all the text of the piece, page by page or panel by panel as the plan orders it: headlines, body text, every product entry (name, code, two to four specification lines, price with its unit), how to order, contact details, and the validity of the prices. Use the facts of the goal and the plan exactly; mark each gap as TODO(client). End with a confirmation list: every price, code, phone number, address and date that appears, for the client to sign off.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Text for every page or panel of the plan, product entries all built the same way, and a confirmation list. No invented fact; no filler.

steps.title: Cover picture
steps.objective: The cover picture of the plan, and only that picture. End with the plan's style line, word for word. Keep the subject in the middle with a calm, empty area where the plan puts the title. No text in the image.

steps.title: Product picture
steps.objective: The product picture of the plan, and only that picture: the product alone, clearly lit, on a plain surface. End with the plan's style line, word for word. No text in the image.

steps.title: Detail picture
steps.objective: The third picture of the plan (a detail, or the product in use), and only that picture. End with the plan's style line, word for word. No text in the image, no people's faces.

steps.title: Layout
steps.objective: Lay the piece out as one self-contained HTML file with print CSS, exactly in the plan's format, grid and tokens, with the copy as written (do not change a name, code, price or number). Pages are fixed-size blocks in millimetres with an @page size; nothing important within 5 mm of an edge; product entries all built the same way and never split across pages. Refer to the three pictures as images/cover.jpg, images/product.jpg and images/detail.jpg. The deliverable is the complete HTML file.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: One complete HTML file that prints at the planned size, holds all the copy unchanged, uses the plan's tokens, and refers to the three pictures by file name.

steps.title: Print handover notes

steps.title: Store strategy

Where the goal leaves a choice open, decide, and say why.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Buyers, the order's path from cart to delivery, a job and a block order for every page, the checkout, payment and shipping as stated assumptions, the scope of the first version, and measures. Every open choice is decided.

steps.title: Art direction and design system
steps.objective: Set the visual direction of the store so that it could only be this client's. Give: the direction in one sentence and what it rules out; the tokens with exact values and a job each (colours in hex with one accent, the type scale with line heights, spacing, radii, borders); how products are photographed and shown; the one strong idea of the home page and of the product page; and the list of real material needed from the client (photographs, logo, texts), each missing one marked TODO(client).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A direction and what it rules out, tokens with exact values, a picture style, one idea per key page, and the material needed. Nothing from the list of things that give machine-made work away.

steps.title: Content and microcopy
steps.objective: Write the words of the store, page by page as the strategy orders them: the home page's headline and blocks; category lines; the product page template (title, description of three to five specific lines, what is in the box, shipping and returns lines); cart and checkout labels, buttons and helper texts; every error and empty state; the order confirmation message; shipping, returns and contact pages. Use the facts of the goal; mark each gap as TODO(client).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Real text for every page of the strategy and for every state (empty, error, out of stock, payment failed and pending). No filler, no invented fact.

steps.title: Pages and states

Include the cart, each checkout step, the order page and the admin's order list.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Every page with its layout at two widths, its components, its real text and every state; touch targets of at least 44 px; text contrast of at least 4.5 to 1.

steps.title: Backend design

steps.acceptanceCriteria: A named stack, a data model, order states, endpoints with errors, payment confirmation by verified notification, stock that cannot be oversold, and admin access with roles.

steps.title: Backend implementation
steps.objective: Implement the backend as designed: the data model with its migrations, every endpoint, the order states, the payment notification handler and the stock rule, with configuration read from the environment and an example file that names each variable without a value. Read the files themselves. Findings most harmful first, each with its place, the harm and the fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with place, harm and fix; what was read and what was not; a verdict.

Point at each place that could be any other shop's, name the rule it breaks and say what to do instead. Say what is good and must be kept. You read code and documents, not a rendered page: say so.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with their place, the rule broken and the change to make, most harmful first; what to keep.

steps.title: Offer and page plan
steps.objective: Plan a landing page for the project goal: who it is for and what they should do on it (one action); the offer in one sentence with what is certain from the goal; the blocks of the page in order, each with its job and the facts it uses; what is left out on purpose; and the facts that are missing, as TODO(client).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: One audience, one action, an offer, an ordered list of blocks with a job each, and the open TODOs. No block without something to say.

steps.title: Art direction
steps.objective: Set the visual direction of the page so that it could only be this client's: the direction in one sentence and what it rules out; tokens with exact values (colours in hex with one accent, type scale, spacing, radii); the one strong idea of the first screen; and the hero picture: what it shows and its style line.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A direction, tokens with exact values, one idea for the first screen, and a hero picture with a style line.

steps.title: Copy
steps.objective: Write the words of the page, block by block as the plan orders them: the headline (at most 10 words: what it is and for whom), the supporting line, each block's text, the button labels, the form labels and messages, and the footer. Facts from the goal only; gaps as TODO(client).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Text for every block of the plan, buttons that say what happens, no filler and no invented fact.

steps.title: Hero picture
steps.objective: The hero picture of the art direction, and only that picture. End with its style line, word for word. Keep the subject in the middle, with a calm, empty area where the headline will sit. No text in the image.

steps.title: Page
steps.objective: Build the page as static HTML and CSS (and only the JavaScript it needs) in site/: site/index.html, site/styles.css, with the tokens of the art direction as CSS custom properties and the copy exactly as written. Refer to the hero picture as site/images/hero.jpg. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A complete page that works at 360 px and on a desktop, with the copy unchanged, visible focus, images with sizes and alt text, and no placeholders.

steps.title: SEO
steps.objective: Give the page's query and intent, its title, meta description, URL, heading outline and JSON-LD, the Open Graph tags for sharing, and what to measure after launch.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: An exact title and description, the outline, JSON-LD that matches the page, sharing tags, and measures.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review the page in site/ against the plan, the art direction and the copy: is every block there with its text unchanged; does anything on it fit another business unchanged; is any fact not from the goal; does it hold at 360 px (read the CSS); are the SEO tags in the page. Read the files themselves. Findings most harmful first, each with its place and its fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with place and fix, what is good, what could not be checked without a browser, and a verdict.

workflows.name: Plugin Minecraft Premium
workflows.description: A Minecraft Java plugin for Paper, built to be sold: the product specification, the technical design, the source in four parts, a test plan, a code review, the documentation and the store page. The source goes to the project workspace. Nothing is compiled or run on a server by this workflow: the test plan says how. Use the team "Plugin Minecraft Premium".

steps.title: Product specification
steps.objective: Write the one-page specification of the plugin for the project goal: who buys it and the problem in their words; the feature as what a player does and sees, step by step; every rule and number behind it; three lists (in the first version, later, never); every option an owner can change, with its default; every command with its arguments and permission; every message a player reads; what it must work with; the target Minecraft and Paper version (what the goal names, otherwise the current stable one, stated as an assumption); and the edge cases to handle.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A buyer, the player's steps, rules with numbers, the three lists, options with defaults, commands with permissions, messages, integrations, a target version and edge cases. Every open choice is decided.

steps.title: Technical design
steps.objective: Design the plugin from the specification: the package and class layout with the job of each class; which work runs on the server thread and which off it; the storage interface, its implementations and the schema; the configuration files with every key; how the configuration is migrated on update; the optional integrations and how their absence is handled; whether Folia is supported and what that costs; the build (Gradle Kotlin DSL, dependencies, what is shaded and relocated).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Classes with a job each, a threading plan, storage with a schema, configuration keys, update migration, integrations, and the build.

steps.title: Project skeleton and configuration
steps.objective: Create the project: settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts, plugin.yml with every command and permission of the specification, config.yml and messages.yml with every key commented, the main class with clean start and stop, and the typed configuration access with the update migration of the design. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The build files, plugin.yml, both configuration files with comments, and a main class that starts and stops cleanly.

steps.title: Core feature
steps.objective: Write the core of the plugin as designed: the services and the listeners that carry out the feature of the specification, with its rules, numbers and edge cases. Read the files of the skeleton first and build on them. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The feature of the specification is implemented with its edge cases; no Bukkit call off the server thread; nothing hard-coded.

steps.title: Commands and messages
steps.objective: Write every command of the specification: arguments with tab completion, the permission check, who may run it (player or console), clear errors for wrong input, and the reload command. Every message comes from messages.yml. Read the existing files first and build on them. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Every command of the specification exists with its permission, tab completion and errors; the reload command works without a restart.

steps.title: Storage and integrations
steps.objective: Write the storage of the design: the interface, the default implementation that works out of the box, the database option with a connection pool, the schema creation and migration, all off the server thread; then the optional integrations of the specification, each switched off with one log line when its plugin is absent. Read the existing files first and build on them. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Storage behind an interface with two implementations, players keyed by UUID, prepared statements, and integrations that are optional.

steps.title: Test plan
steps.objective: Write the test plan for the plugin: the unit tests worth having, with their cases; and the manual test list for a real Paper server, each test with what to do and what should happen: fresh install, each command as player, as console and without permission, wrong arguments, a second player, a reload, a restart in the middle of an action, a missing optional plugin, a broken configuration file, an update from an older configuration. Read the source in the workspace first. Say that nothing was run.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Unit test cases, a manual test list that covers every command and every edge case of the specification, and what was not run.

steps.title: Code review
steps.objective: Review the source in the workspace against the specification, the design and the skills of this team. Read the files themselves. Look for: Bukkit calls off the server thread or blocking calls on it; messages or numbers not in a file; missing permission checks; player names used as keys; tasks and connections not closed on disable; configuration that an update would wipe; code that is named and not written. Findings most harmful first, each with file and line, the harm and the fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with file and line, harm and fix; what is good; what was read and not run; a verdict.

steps.title: Documentation
steps.objective: Write the README of the plugin from the specification and the files in the workspace: what it does; requirements (server software and version, Java); installation in numbered steps; the commands and permissions table; the configuration reference with every key, type, default and meaning; placeholders and integrations; troubleshooting by symptom; how to build from source; how to get support. Document what is in the files; mark what you could not confirm as TODO(author).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A README with installation steps, a complete commands and permissions table, a complete configuration reference and troubleshooting.

steps.title: Store page and changelog
steps.objective: Write the store page of the plugin, ready to paste: the first lines (what it does and for whom, without adjectives); three to five features, each one sentence that names something visible in the game; requirements and what is not supported; what the price includes (as TODO(client) for the numbers); the list of screenshots or clips to make, with what each shows; and the changelog entry for version 1.0.0. No invented downloads, reviews or server names.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A store page with features, requirements, limits, a media list and a changelog entry. No invented proof.

workflows.name: Addon Minecraft Premium
workflows.description: An add-on for Minecraft Bedrock Edition: the concept, the technical design, the behavior pack, the resource pack, the scripts, a test list, a review, the documentation with packaging steps, and the listing. The packs go to the project workspace as text files; textures and icons are listed for a person to add, and nothing is run in the game by this workflow. Use the team "Addon Minecraft Premium".

steps.title: Concept and content list
steps.objective: Write the concept of the add-on for the project goal: who it is for and what it adds, as what a player does and sees; the content list (every item, block, entity, recipe and mechanic, each with its numbers and how a survival player gets it); what it does not touch in the vanilla game; three lists (in the first version, later, never); the target Minecraft Bedrock version (what the goal names, otherwise the current stable one, stated as an assumption); and whether anything needs an experiment or a beta API, with the stable alternative.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: An audience, the player's view, a content list with numbers and a fair way to get each thing, the three lists and a target version.

steps.title: Technical design
steps.objective: Design the add-on from the concept: the names of the two pack folders; the namespace; a table of every identifier with the files it appears in (definition, texture key, language key); the format version used for each kind of file; the script modules and their versions, or why there are no scripts; the list of textures and icons with path, size in pixels and what each shows; and the four UUIDs or more that the manifests need, written out, all different.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Pack names, a namespace, an identifier table, format versions, script modules, a texture list, and real, different UUIDs.

steps.title: Behavior pack
steps.objective: Write the behavior pack as designed: manifest.json with the UUIDs of the design and the dependency on the resource pack, every item, block and entity definition of the concept, the recipes and loot tables, the functions, and the language files. Valid JSON only. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A manifest with the designed UUIDs and dependencies, and a definition for everything in the content list, in valid JSON.

steps.title: Resource pack
steps.objective: Write the resource pack as designed: manifest.json with its UUIDs and the dependency on the behavior pack, item_texture.json, terrain_texture.json and blocks.json for every identifier of the design, the client entity files, and the language files with a name for everything. Read the behavior pack's files first so that every identifier matches. Textures are not written: keep the design's texture list up to date. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A manifest, a texture key and a name for every identifier of the behavior pack, in valid JSON.

steps.title: Scripts
steps.objective: Write the scripts of the design: the entry file named in the manifest and its modules, subscribing to events rather than polling, with everything that can be missing guarded. If the design has no scripts, answer in one line that this part does not apply and why, and change nothing. Read the behavior pack's manifest first: the script module and its dependencies must be in it. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The scripts of the design exist and are named in the manifest with their module dependencies; or the part does not apply, with the reason.

steps.title: Test list
steps.objective: Write the test list for the person who runs the add-on in the game, each test with what to do and what should happen: the Content Log on and empty at world load; each item, block and entity present with its texture and its name; each recipe and interaction in survival; each script event; leaving and rejoining; a second player. Read the packs in the workspace first. Say that nothing was run.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A test for everything in the content list and for loading without errors, and what was not run.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review the packs in the workspace against the concept, the design and the skills of this team. Read the files themselves. Check: every UUID different and the dependencies pointing at header UUIDs; every identifier present in every place the design's table says; valid JSON; a format version in each file that allows the components used; no custom content in the minecraft namespace; any beta API named. Findings most harmful first, each with file and place, the harm and the fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with file and place, harm and fix; what is good; what was read and not run; a verdict.

steps.title: Documentation and packaging
steps.objective: Write the README of the add-on from the concept and the files in the workspace: what it adds; the game version and any experiment needed; installation; how each item and block is obtained; known limits; the list of textures and icons a person still has to add, with sizes; the steps to package the two folders as .mcpack files and one .mcaddon; and the changelog entry for version 1.0.0.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A README with installation, content, limits, the textures still to add, packaging steps and a changelog entry.

steps.title: Listing
steps.objective: Write the listing of the add-on, ready to paste: the first lines (what it adds and for whom, without adjectives); three to five features, each one sentence that names something visible in the game; the game version and what is needed; what it does not do; and the list of screenshots to make, with what each shows. No invented downloads or reviews.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A listing with features, requirements, limits and a media list. No invented proof.

workflows.name: Setup Server Minecraft
workflows.description: A Minecraft server planned and handed over as documents a person follows: software and sizing, the configuration, the plugin stack and permissions, security and backups, the deployment on the host or panel, the launch checklist, a review and the handover document. Nothing is installed by this workflow. Use the team "Setup Server Minecraft".

steps.title: Intake, software and sizing
steps.objective: Plan the server for the project goal. Write down what the goal says and what you assume: edition and version, game mode, players at peak, one server or a network, Java only or Bedrock players too, where it runs and with how much memory and CPU, who administers it. Then decide, with reasons: the server software (and the proxy and Geyser where needed), the memory for the heap and what is left outside it, the world border and pre-generation, and the ports.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: What is known and assumed, a software choice with reasons, heap and container memory that fit together, pre-generation, and the ports.

steps.title: Configuration
steps.objective: Give the configuration of the server as tables of file, key, value and reason, for each file that changes from its default: server.properties, the Paper configuration, spigot.yml, bukkit.yml, and the proxy's where there is one. Name the gameplay cost of every performance setting. Give the start command with the memory values of the plan; take the JVM flags from the Paper documentation and say where they came from, or say that they are to be taken from there.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A table for each file with a reason for every value, the gameplay cost of each performance setting, and a start command whose flags have a named source.

steps.title: Plugin stack and permissions
steps.objective: Choose the plugins: a small set of maintained ones, each with its job, whether it is free, and what breaks without it; say for each whether you could check that it supports the server version. Then design the permission groups (default, member, moderator, admin) with what each may do, without wildcards for staff, and the first settings of each plugin that matter.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A plugin list with a job each and a version check or a note that it could not be checked, permission groups, and first settings.

steps.title: Security and backups
steps.objective: Write the security and backup plan: who can join as whom (online mode, or a proxy with secured forwarding and backends closed to the internet); operators and staff access; the firewall as a list of ports with protocol and reason; RCON and the database; where each secret is generated and kept, never its value; the update policy; and the backups: what, how often, how many, where off the machine, and the restore rehearsal.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Join security, staff access, a port list, secrets by place and not by value, an update policy, and backups with a rehearsed restore.

steps.title: Deployment
steps.objective: Write the steps to put the server up where the plan says it runs (a panel such as Pterodactyl, or a VPS): each step with what to do, and a check that shows it worked. On a panel: the egg or image and Java version, the start-up command and its variables, the memory limit that fits the heap, the allocations (TCP for Java, UDP for Bedrock players), and which files to edit in the file manager. End with accepting the Minecraft EULA, which the owner does themselves.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Numbered steps with a check after each, the memory limit and heap set together, the allocations, and the EULA left to the owner.

steps.title: Launch checklist
steps.objective: Write the launch checklist, each item with what to do and what should be seen: a start without errors in the log; tick times in the profiler; joining as a default player and trying what they must not be able to do; a griefing attempt at spawn; killing the process and starting again; restoring a backup to a test server; a Bedrock player joining where the plan has them. Read the documents in the workspace first.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A checklist that covers start-up, performance, permissions, protection, crash recovery and restore, each item with its expected result.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review the configuration, the plugin stack, the security plan and the deployment steps against the plan and the skills of this team: a setting with no reason; a value that contradicts another document; a secret written down; a port open that nothing needs; a step without a check; a plugin whose support for the version was not checked; a list of flags with no source. Findings most harmful first, each with its place and its fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with place and fix, what is good, what could not be verified, and a verdict.

steps.title: Handover document
steps.objective: Write the handover document for the owner from the documents in the workspace: how to start, stop and update the server; where each configuration file is and what the important settings mean; the staff groups; how backups run and how to restore one; what to look at first when it lags; where the secrets are kept (not the secrets); what was assumed and not verified; and what the owner still has to do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Day-to-day operation, update and restore steps, the staff groups, where secrets are kept, the assumptions, and the owner's to-do list.

workflows.name: Fitur Minecraft Custom
workflows.description: A custom Minecraft feature on whichever platform fits: the specification decides between a Java plugin, a Bedrock add-on and server configuration, and the steps for the parts that do not apply say so in a line. Then a test list, a review and the documentation. Use the team "Developer Minecraft".

steps.title: Specification and platform
steps.objective: Write the specification of the feature for the project goal: what a player does and sees, step by step; every rule and number; the options an owner can change, with defaults; the commands and permissions; the edge cases. Then decide the platform, with the reason: which of a Java plugin (Paper), a Bedrock add-on, and server configuration are needed, one or several. State for each of the three whether it applies, and the game version targeted.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The player's steps, rules, options, commands and edge cases, and a clear yes or no for each of the three parts, with a version.

steps.title: Java plugin part
steps.objective: If the specification says the Java plugin part applies: design it in a few lines, then write the complete plugin: build files, plugin.yml, configuration and messages files, and every class. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do. If the specification says it does not apply, answer in one line that this part does not apply and why, and write nothing.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The complete plugin of the specification; or one line saying the part does not apply.

steps.title: Bedrock add-on part
steps.objective: If the specification says the Bedrock add-on part applies: design it in a few lines (namespace, identifiers, UUIDs), then write both packs complete: manifests, definitions, texture mapping and language files, scripts where needed, and the list of textures to add. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do. If the specification says it does not apply, answer in one line that this part does not apply and why, and write nothing.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Both packs of the specification, in valid JSON; or one line saying the part does not apply.

steps.title: Server configuration part
steps.objective: Write what must be set up on the server for the feature to work: plugins to install with the settings that matter, permissions to grant to which group, settings to change as file, key, value and reason, and anything a Bedrock player needs. Read what the developers wrote first. If nothing has to be set up beyond installing what was built, say so and give the installation steps.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The server-side steps with a reason for each setting; or the installation steps alone.

steps.title: Test list
steps.objective: Write the test list for the feature, each test with what to do and what should happen, for each part that applies: on a Paper server for the plugin, in the game with the Content Log on for the add-on, and the server settings. Cover every step, rule and edge case of the specification. Read the files in the workspace first. Say that nothing was run.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A test for every rule and edge case of the specification, for each part that applies, and what was not run.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review what was built against the specification. Read the files themselves. For a plugin: threads, hard-coded values, permission checks, cleanup on disable, incomplete code. For an add-on: UUIDs, identifiers in every place, valid JSON, format versions. Findings most harmful first, each with file and place, the harm and the fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with file and place, harm and fix; what is good; what was read and not run; a verdict.

steps.title: Documentation
steps.objective: Write the README for the feature from the specification and the files in the workspace: what it does; what is needed (edition, version, server software); installation for each part that applies; the commands, permissions and options as tables; known limits; and what a person still has to do (compile, add textures, package).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A README with installation for each part, complete tables, limits, and what is left to do.

workflows.name: Install Panel + Wings Pterodactyl
workflows.description: The runbooks for installing the Pterodactyl Panel and Wings on a customer's Linux server: intake and plan, the Panel, Wings and the first node, network and TLS, hardening and backups, verification and troubleshooting, a review, and the customer handover. Nothing is run on a server by this workflow: a technician follows the runbooks. Use the team "Install Panel + Wings Pterodactyl".

steps.title: Intake and plan
steps.objective: Write the intake and the plan for the project goal. What the goal says and what you assume: the operating system and version of each machine, the architecture, root or sudo access, whether Docker can run there (the kind of virtualisation), one machine or separate ones, the domain names for the Panel and for each node, whether anything sits behind a proxy or CDN, and what will be hosted. Then the plan: the DNS records to create, the ports to open, the order of the work, what to back up first, and the questions the customer must answer before the work starts, each with the default you used. Say which official documentation pages you read, or that you could not read them.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Known facts and assumptions, the Docker check, DNS records, ports, the order of work, open questions with defaults, and the documentation that was or was not read.

steps.title: Panel runbook
steps.objective: Write the runbook for installing the Panel on the planned operating system, following the official documentation: dependencies; the database and its user; downloading the Panel; the environment set-up; the application key and its backup; the database migration; the first administrator (the customer types the password); file ownership; the scheduler entry; the queue worker service; the web server configuration with TLS. Every step: the command in a code block, what it does, and a check that shows it worked. No secret is written: <generated>, and where it is kept. Mark every version or package name you could not verify.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Numbered steps with a command and a check each, the application key backed up, the scheduler and the queue worker both set up, no secret written, and everything unverified marked.

steps.title: Wings and first node runbook
steps.objective: Write the runbook for Wings on the planned machine, following the official documentation: Docker; the Wings binary; creating the location and the node in the Panel with the right name, scheme and ports; putting the node's configuration from the Panel on the machine; the first start in the foreground and what its output should say; the service; allocations; and one small test server, created and started. Every step with a command or a click path, and a check.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Numbered steps with a check each, the node's configuration taken from the Panel and not written by hand, a foreground start before the service, allocations, and a test server.

steps.title: Network, DNS, TLS and firewall
steps.objective: Write the network part: the DNS records and how to check that each resolves; the certificates for the Panel's name and for each node's name, with unattended renewal that reloads the service that uses them; the firewall rules of the machine and of the provider as a table of port, protocol, source and reason (web, the Wings daemon port, SFTP, the allocation ranges); what must not be proxied by a CDN; and a check from outside the machine that lists which ports answer. Before any firewall is enabled, the step says to keep the current session open and test a second one.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: DNS with checks, certificates that renew and reload, a firewall table, the CDN rule, an outside check, and the lock-out warning.

steps.title: Hardening and backups
steps.objective: Write the hardening and backup part for these machines: access by SSH key with a tested second session before passwords are switched off; automatic security updates and the reboot plan; services that return after a reboot; the database and cache on localhost; two-factor sign-in for Panel administrators; where each secret is kept and how it is rotated; and the backups: the Panel's database and its environment file with the application key, off the machine, daily, with a restore tried once. Each step with a command and a check. State what this baseline does not cover.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Steps with a check each, the lock-out warning, secrets by place and not by value, backups that include the application key with a tried restore, and what is not covered.

steps.title: Verification and troubleshooting
steps.objective: Write the verification checklist to run after the installation, each item with the command or click and what should be seen: the Panel signs in over HTTPS; the scheduler and the queue worker run; the node shows as connected; a server installs, starts and is reachable from outside; SFTP works; everything is back after a reboot. Then the troubleshooting table: symptom, likely causes, and the command that tells which, for at least: node offline, Panel error 500, a 502 or blank page, servers stuck installing, a game server not reachable, SFTP refusing the login.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A verification checklist with expected results, including a reboot, and a troubleshooting table of at least six symptoms with the command that confirms each cause.

steps.title: Runbook review
steps.objective: Review the runbooks as the technician who must follow them on a customer's server. Read the files themselves. For every step: is there a check; is the command complete and in the right order; is anything guessed or marked unverified; is a secret written anywhere; would it survive a reboot; do the firewall ports match the ports the node uses; could a step lock the operator out. Findings most harmful first, each with file and step, the harm and the fix. List everything that must be confirmed against the official documentation before use.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with file and step, harm and fix; the list to confirm against the official documentation; what is good; a verdict.

steps.title: Customer handover
steps.objective: Write the handover document for the customer from the documents in the workspace: what was installed and where (addresses, folders, services, accounts by name, never passwords); where the secrets are kept; how to add a server, an allocation and a user; how to update the Panel and Wings, with a backup first; what is backed up and how to restore it; what was assumed and not verified; and what the customer still has to do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: What was installed, where secrets are kept, day-to-day tasks, update and restore, the assumptions, and the customer's to-do list. No secret in it.

workflows.name: Bot Discord
workflows.description: A Discord bot: its design, the source, a test list, a code review, and the documentation with deployment notes. The source goes to the project workspace; nothing is run by this workflow. Use the team "Bot Discord".

steps.title: Design
steps.objective: Design the bot for the project goal: the slash commands as a table (name, options, who may use it, whether the reply is private); the events it listens to; the intents, the smallest set that works, with the reason for each; the permissions its invite asks for; what data it keeps, where, and how it is deleted; what the user sees when something fails; the library and runtime with their versions (what the goal names, otherwise discord.js on a current Node.js LTS, stated as an assumption); and the file layout.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A command table, events, minimal intents with reasons, invite permissions, data kept and deleted, failure messages, versions, and the file layout.

steps.title: Source
steps.objective: Write the bot as designed: the entry point, one file per command and per event, the script that registers the commands, the storage, .env.example with the names of the variables and no values, package.json, and a .gitignore that keeps the environment file out. Every interaction is answered in time; every handler catches its errors; mentions from user input are off. Write complete, working files into the project workspace. Answer with the list of the files you wrote, how to build or run and test them, and what you could not do.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Every command and event of the design exists; the token comes from the environment only; no interaction is left unanswered.

steps.title: Test list
steps.objective: Write the test list for the bot, each test with what to do and what should happen: each command with valid and invalid input, without the permission, in a direct message, with the bot's role too low, and after a restart; the bot joining and leaving a server; the database or Discord being slow. Read the source in the workspace first. Say that nothing was run.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A test for every command and failure of the design, and what was not run.

steps.title: Code review
steps.objective: Review the source in the workspace against the design. Read the files themselves. Look for: a privileged intent that is not needed; a path where an interaction is not answered in time; a secret in code or logs; user input that can cause a mention, a crash or an unintended action; handlers without error handling; code that is named and not written. Findings most harmful first, each with file and line, the harm and the fix.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with file and line, harm and fix; what is good; what was read and not run; a verdict.

steps.title: Documentation and deployment
steps.objective: Write the README of the bot from the design and the files in the workspace: creating the application and the bot in Discord's developer portal; which intents to switch on; the invite link with its scopes and permissions; the environment variables; registering the commands; running it; and deployment where the client hosts it: a process manager or a container that restarts on failure, or on a game panel the Node.js image, the start command and the variables. End with the commands table.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Set-up in the developer portal, intents, the invite, variables, registration, running, deployment notes and a commands table. No token in it.

workflows.name: Konten Carousel
workflows.description: A carousel of five square slides for a social media feed: the plan with the words of every slide, the five pictures, the caption with hashtags and alt text, and a review. The words are set on the pictures afterwards: generated pictures carry no lettering. Use the team "Konten Media Sosial".

steps.title: Carousel plan
steps.objective: Plan a carousel of exactly 5 square slides for the project goal. Give: the audience in one line; the goal of the post (reach, trust or sale) and the one action it asks for; one style line that fixes the look of all five pictures; then for each slide: the headline (five to seven words), the body (at most twenty words, or none), the picture (what it shows), and where the text sits on it (which area of the picture stays calm and empty). Slide 1 is the cover and must make sense alone; slide 5 is the summary and the action. Facts from the goal only; gaps as TODO(client).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: An audience, one goal and one action, a style line, and exactly 5 numbered slides, each with a headline, a body, a picture and a place for the text. No invented fact.

steps.title: Slide 1 picture
steps.objective: The picture of slide 1 of the plan, and only that slide. End with the plan's style line, word for word, so that the five pictures belong together. Leave the area that the plan names for the text calm and empty. No text, no lettering and no logos in the image.

steps.title: Slide 2 picture
steps.objective: The picture of slide 2 of the plan, and only that slide. End with the plan's style line, word for word, so that the five pictures belong together. Leave the area that the plan names for the text calm and empty. No text, no lettering and no logos in the image.

steps.title: Slide 3 picture
steps.objective: The picture of slide 3 of the plan, and only that slide. End with the plan's style line, word for word, so that the five pictures belong together. Leave the area that the plan names for the text calm and empty. No text, no lettering and no logos in the image.

steps.title: Slide 4 picture
steps.objective: The picture of slide 4 of the plan, and only that slide. End with the plan's style line, word for word, so that the five pictures belong together. Leave the area that the plan names for the text calm and empty. No text, no lettering and no logos in the image.

steps.title: Slide 5 picture
steps.objective: The picture of slide 5 of the plan, and only that slide. End with the plan's style line, word for word, so that the five pictures belong together. Leave the area that the plan names for the text calm and empty. No text, no lettering and no logos in the image.

steps.title: Caption, hashtags and alt text
steps.objective: Write what goes with the carousel: the caption (the first line carries the point, then two or three short lines of what the slides do not say, then the one action of the plan); 3 to 8 hashtags the audience searches; one line of alt text for each of the five slides; and a suggestion for the first comment.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A caption that opens with the point and ends with the plan's action, 3 to 8 hashtags, five alt texts, and a first comment.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review the carousel plan and the caption against the project goal and the skills of this team: one point a slide and one action; a cover that makes sense alone; word counts within the limits; any fact, price or result that is not in the goal; any phrase from the lists of words to cut. Quote each phrase you object to and give the rewritten line. Say that the pictures themselves were not seen.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with the quoted phrase and its rewrite, what is good, what was not seen, and a verdict.

workflows.name: Artikel SEO
workflows.description: An article that answers what people search for: the query, intent and outline; the draft; the SEO pass with title, description and structured data; and a review. Use the team "Artikel SEO".

steps.title: Query, intent and outline
steps.objective: Plan an article for the project goal: the main query a person types and two or three close variants; what they want when they type it; what would satisfy them that the usual results do not give; the outline as headings in the order a reader asks; for each heading the point to make and the fact, example or table it needs; and what must come from the client, as TODO(client). Say that the choice of query is a reasoned assumption until it is measured.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A query with variants and intent, what makes the article worth reading, an outline with a point and a source for each heading, and the open TODOs.

steps.title: Draft
steps.objective: Write the article from the outline, in the language of the goal: the answer in the first paragraph; one point a section; examples with real numbers where the goal gives them; a clear recommendation and for whom. No fact, statistic or quote that the goal or the outline does not give: mark each gap as TODO(client). No filler opening, no summary that repeats the text.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: An article that follows the outline, answers the query in its first paragraph, and has no invented fact and no filler.

steps.title: SEO pass
steps.objective: Give what the article needs to be found: the title (50 to 60 characters), the meta description (120 to 155 characters), the URL, the final heading outline, the JSON-LD (Article with headline, dates and author as TODO(client), and FAQPage only for questions the text really answers), image file names and alt texts, internal links in and out by the words they are set on, and the edits to the draft that would help a searcher, each quoted with its replacement. No keyword stuffing.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: An exact title, description and URL, the JSON-LD, links, and quoted edits.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review the article against the project goal and the skills of this team: does the first paragraph answer the query; is every fact from the goal or marked TODO; are there phrases from the lists of words to cut (quote each and give the rewritten line); does the structured data match the text. Findings most harmful first.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: Findings with the quoted phrase and its rewrite, a check of every fact against its source, and a verdict.

workflows.name: Proposal & Penawaran
workflows.description: A service proposal or quotation a client can say yes to: needs and scope, the proposal with options and a price table, the polished text, and a review. Prices come from the project goal; a missing one stays a TODO. Use the team "Proposal & Penawaran".

steps.title: Needs and scope
steps.objective: Work out what is to be offered for the project goal: the client's situation and the result they want, in their words; what the goal says about volume, deadline and budget, and what it does not say; the scope as deliverables a client can check; what is not included; what is needed from the client; the questions that would change the scope, each with the assumption used; and every price, name, date and legal detail the goal gives, listed, with each missing one as TODO(provider).
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The need in the client's words, deliverables, exclusions, what the client must provide, open questions with assumptions, and the facts given and missing.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.objective: Write the proposal from the scope, two to four pages: the summary; what the client asked for; what will be done, as deliverables; what is not included; at most three options named by what they are, with the recommended one and why; the timeline with what is needed from the client at each step; the price table (item, what it includes, quantity, unit price, amount) with subtotal, tax treatment and total; payment schedule and methods; the validity of the offer; the terms that prevent disputes (revisions, acceptance, support, changes of scope, ownership); and one next step. Prices from the scope only; a missing one stays TODO(provider). Check that the totals add up.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: A proposal with every section, options named by what they are, a price table whose totals add up or carry a TODO, terms, and one next step. No invented price or client.

steps.title: Polish
steps.objective: Edit the proposal so that a client who is not technical can read it in one go: plain words, short sentences, the same name for the same thing everywhere, no promise the provider cannot keep. Do not change a number, a date, a deliverable or a term. The deliverable is the complete edited proposal.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The complete proposal, clearer, with every number, date, deliverable and term unchanged.

steps.title: Review
steps.objective: Review the final proposal as the client's cautious partner: can they tell exactly what they get, by when, for how much and what is extra; does every number come from the project goal or carry a TODO; do the totals add up (do the arithmetic); did the polish change any number or term (compare the two versions); is there one next step; what would they object to. Findings most harmful first.
steps.acceptanceCriteria: The arithmetic checked, every number traced to its source, differences between the two versions, objections, and a verdict.
